newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Tourists, honeymooners were on crashed airliner.
newsitem.headline: Tourists, honeymooners were on crashed airliner.

text.p: A Korean Air Lines (KAL) jumbo jet that crashed on the Pacific island of Guam on Wednesday was carrying mostly South Korean honeymooners and holidaymakers among its 231 passengers, airline officials said.
The Boeing 747-300 aircraft, with 23 crew, crashed in a hilly jungle area about three miles (five km) south of Agana International Airport on a scheduled flight from Seoul.
Also aboard Flight 801 were 13 foreigners, mostly Americans, three infants and a prominent South Korean member of parliament, airline official Kwon Woong-min said.
Guam and other Pacific islands are popular destinations for South Korean honeymooners.

Officials said Shin Ki-ha, a four-term lawmaker and former parliamentary leader of the main opposition National Congress for New Politics, his wife and about 20 party members were on the plane. South Korean Construction and Transportation Minister Lee Hwan-kyun said at least 50 people appeared to have survived the crash, and that he expected the number to rise.
But one airline official said rescue operations were being hampered by darkness and rugged terrain that prevented vehicles getting close.
"The crash site is a rugged valley where an oil pipe is running through," Oh Boo-geun, a South Korean resident in Guam, told Korea Broadcasting System (KBS).
Oh said he walked close to the scene and saw smoke shrouding the wreckage of the plane. He said U.S. military helicopters were helping to rescue survivors.
KBS, quoting air controllers in Guam, said the captain of the Korean airliner said the words "Something wrong" shortly before he lost contact with them.
The South Korean Foreign Ministry said it would soon dispatch a fact-finding mission to Guam.
The U.S. Defense Department said it would also fly a National Transportation Safety Board team to Guam to investigate the crash.
